newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Canberra against higher foreign media investment.
newsitem.headline: Canberra against higher foreign media investment.

text.p: Australian Prime Minster John Howard said on Friday the government did not want higher foreign media investment.
"In the media for example, which is in the news at the moment, we've made it clear we don't want foreign investment to go any higher," Howard said in an interview Sydney radio 2UE.
Analysts say publisher John Fairfax Holdings Ltd, one of Australia's largest media companies, is a takeover target because no long term major investors have taken a stake in the company.
But Australia has two sets of restrictions on media ownership, and some investors have said it can afford to keep only one of them unless it wants to force capital away from the industry.
One set of restrictions holds down foreign investment in the media, forbidding foreigners from controlling media.
The other limits so-called cross ownership within the industry by forbidding one person from controlling both television and newspapers in the same market.
Media mogul Kerry Packer, who holds 12 percent Fairfax, has proposed to merge the company with his Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd (PBL).
PBL, however, owns the Nine Network Australia, a television broadcaster with stations in Sydney and Melbourne, where Fairfax's main newspapers are based.
